chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We're going to introduce a new kind of statistic now called rolling statistics.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And as opposed to, say, just taking the mean across a whole period of time,

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: we take sort of a snapshot over Windows.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And I'm going to show you what that means in just a moment.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: Now on that last slide, we computed a global mean,

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: which would be something about like this on this data.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: A rolling mean is a little bit different, and here's how it works.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: Let's suppose we're going to take a 20-day rolling mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We go starting from here, 20 days, so right about here.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And then we take the mean of all that data behind us.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We can draw a little box around that.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: This is called the window.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: In our case, it's 20 days.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: So we average all these values, and we get one mean, which is this point.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We then move the window forward one day, and we take another mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: Here's our next mean, which is a little bit higher.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: Now if we do that every day over this entire year, so

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: this is S&P 500 over the year 2012, we get something that looks about like this.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: You can see essentially that it's a line that follows the day-to-day values of whatever it is we're tracking,

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: but it lags a little bit.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: It's sort of a smoothed and lagged line.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And this is called the rolling mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We can compute statistics like this, just like the rolling mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We could do standard deviation.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: We could do mode, median, and so on.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: All of those statistics I showed you just a moment ago can also be used as rolling statistics.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: In a lesson in the next mini-course, we're going to spend a lot of time talking about technical indicators.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And this is actually one of them, this rolling mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: It's called by technical analysts a simple moving average.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And one thing they look at is places where the price crosses through the rolling average.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: So in this case, the price is moving down through the 20-day mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: Now a hypothesis that I'm not saying I support, but a hypothesis that many who conduct technical analysis,

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: is that this rolling mean may be a good representation of sort of the true underlying price of a stock.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: And that significant deviations from that, like this one here, eventually result in a return to the mean.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: So if you can look for, say, significant deviations like this one, you might find, say, a buying opportunity here.

chunks.title: Rolling statistics
chunks.text: A challenge, though, is to know, hey, when is that deviation significant enough that you should pay attention to it?
